Kuvitus: laboratorion pöydällä on säädet: Illustration: on a laboratory bench there is an adjustable voltage source, from which a red and a black lead take the current to a breadboard. On the board are four LEDs side by side at the same voltage. The red and yellow LEDs shine brightly and send out their light as wavy lines, the green one glows dimly, and the blue LED is dark.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: LEDin puoli: Schematic figure, not to scale: the energy bands of the semiconductor of an LED. Energy is on the vertical axis. At the top is the conduction band and at the bottom the valence band, and between them is the energy gap E g, at whose energies an electron cannot have a state. The vertical dashed line is the interface: on the left is the n region, whose conduction band contains blue electrons e minus, and on the right the p region, whose valence band contains empty places, that is holes, as white circles. At the interface an electron falls from the conduction band into a hole of the valence band, and from there a red wavy arrow, a photon, goes to the right; its energy hf is approximately equal to the energy gap.
Kuvaaja: kolmen valonlähteen spektri sam: Graph: the spectra of three light sources on the same wavelength axis, 380–720 nanometres, with relative intensity on the vertical axis. The spectrum of the incandescent lamp is continuous: an orange curve rises steadily from violet to red. The spectrum of the red LED is a narrow peak at a wavelength of 630 nanometres, and its width is about 20 nanometres. The spectrum of the red laser diode is a very narrow line at a wavelength of 650 nanometres, with a width of about 1 nanometre (the figure is only indicative, not to scale). The peaks of the LED and the laser diode have been scaled to the same height, and the curve of the incandescent lamp lower.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kolmen LEDin virt: Graph to scale: the current of three LEDs in milliamperes as a function of voltage, voltage axis 0–3.5 volts. The current of the red LED is almost zero up to about 1.8 volts and then grows linearly. The curve of the green LED has the same shape but is further to the right, and that of the blue one still further right. The straight part of each curve has been extended with a dashed line to the voltage axis, and the point of intersection is the threshold voltage U k of the LED: 1.88 volts for the red, 2.30 for the green and 2.52 for the blue.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: kuuden LEDin kynn: Graph to scale: the threshold voltage U k in volts of six LEDs as a function of the frequency f of their light, frequency axis from zero to 8 times 10 to the power 14 hertz. The points have the colours of the LEDs: red 4.76 and 1.88; orange 4.96 and 1.95; yellow 5.08 and 2.00; green 5.71 and 2.30; blue 6.38 and 2.52; violet 7.40 and 2.95, with the frequencies in units of 10 to the power 14 hertz and the voltages in volts.

Graph to scale: the threshold voltage U k in volts of six LEDs as a function of the frequency f of their light, frequency axis from zero to 8 times 10 to the power 14 hertz. The points have the colours of the LEDs: red 4.76 and 1.88; orange 4.96 and 1.95; yellow 5.08 and 2.00; green 5.71 and 2.30; blue 6.38 and 2.52; violet 7.40 and 2.95, with the frequencies in units of 10 to the power 14 hertz and the voltages in volts. A line has been fitted to the points; it continues as a dashed line close to the origin and cuts the vertical axis slightly below zero. A triangle showing the slope has been drawn on the line, and the label says that the slope k is h divided by e.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa ruutupaperilla: LE: Graph to scale on graph paper: the threshold voltage U k in volts of LEDs from 1.5 to 3.5 as a function of the frequency f of their light, frequency axis from 4.0 to 8.0 times 10 to the power 14 hertz. The vertical grid lines are 0.2 times 10 to the power 14 hertz apart and the horizontal ones 0.1 volt apart. Six measured points and a line fitted to them, which passes exactly through the intersections of grid lines at frequency 4.6 and voltage 1.80 and at frequency 7.0 and voltage 2.80.
